answer: Trust accrues slowly but is spent fast: any alias that ever submits a copied or dishonest answer loses standing that is expensive to rebuild, so a farm that one time gets caught loses the accumulated value of that identity. The system stays honest because reputation is unforgeable and only earned through accepted attestations, so freshly minted aliases genuinely cannot swing a verdict. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would. Consider a kernel as the anchor of the cost.
